n1.text: You enter the Whispering Forest. A tired old badger blocks the path. He looks grumpy. What do you say?

choices.text: Excuse me, sir. Would you mind letting us pass?

choices.explain: Rude, and 'want go' should be 'want to go'.

n1b.text: The badger huffs and sits down even harder. 'Manners, little traveller!' Try again.

choices.text: I'm sorry. Could you possibly let us through, please?

n2.text: The badger smiles. 'Two paths lie ahead. The left one is shorter, but its bridge is broken. The right one is longer, but safe.' Which do you choose?

choices.text: We'd better take the right path, even though it's longer.
choices.explain: 'had better' + verb; 'even though' contrasts two facts.

choices.text: If we would take the left path, we will be faster.
choices.explain: No 'would' in the if-clause: 'If we take…, we'll be faster.'

n2b.text: You reach the broken bridge and get your boots soaked. Splash! You trudge back to the fork.

choices.text: OK, let's go the safe way this time.
choices.explain: Learning from mistakes is part of every quest!

n3.text: A lost fairy is crying beside a glowing mushroom. 'I've lost my lantern!' she sobs.

choices.text: Don't worry. When did you last see it?
choices.explain: Reassure, then ask a helpful past simple question.
Past questions need 'did': 'Where did you lose it?'

n3b.text: The fairy looks confused. 'Pardon?' Ask her properly.

n4.text: 'I had it when I was dancing by the stream,' she says. At the stream you find the lantern caught in the reeds.

choices.text: Here it is! It must have fallen while you were dancing.
choices.explain: 'must have + past participle' = a confident guess about the past.

choices.text: Here it is! It must fall when you dance.
choices.explain: For a past deduction use 'must have fallen'.

end.text: The fairy's lantern glows golden. 'Thank you, kind traveller!' She gives you a Forest Star. Quest complete!
